title: David
lead: Israel's second king, about 1000 BC: the shepherd from Bethlehem who became the model king, traditionally credited with many psalms, and the ancestor of the promised Messiah, who is called "the son of David."

sections.b: David is anointed as a boy in Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16), defeats Goliath (1 Samuel 17), flees Saul (1 Samuel 19–30), and becomes king first of Judah and then of all Israel, ruling from Jerusalem (2 Samuel 2–5). God promises him a lasting dynasty (2 Samuel 7:12–16). His sin with Bathsheba and the troubles that follow are told without hiding anything (2 Samuel 11–20). About 73 psalms carry his name in their titles, though how many he wrote is debated. The prophets hope for a coming king from his line (Isaiah 11:1; Jeremiah 23:5; Ezekiel 34:23–24), and the New Testament opens by calling Jesus "the son of David" (Matthew 1:1).
